(A tourism guide penned by the Pioneer Association. But the column about Egla Town hasn't been updated in quite a while.)

[The Next Big Travel Hot Spot]: Egla Town!
For those brave enough to venture to the place that inspired the adventurous plays during the Carnevale, exploring the legendary realm of the mighty "giant," listening to the songs echoing from the sea of clouds by the water, or following in the footsteps of knights in pursuit of honor and justice will no longer be mere fantasies. In Egla Town, travelers can immerse themselves in breathtaking waterside scenery, observe the majestic migration of Tumbleyaks, and watch windmills spin gracefully on the plains, while bathing in the golden light of the setting sun. Alternatively, they can simply enjoy a peaceful afternoon tea and indulge in century-old delicacies, all while being surrounded by the vibrant colors of blooming flowers.

[Dreamy Destinations] Nimbus Sanctum!
In this edition of [Dreamy Destinations], we journey to the mesmerizing Nimbus Sanctum hidden deep within Whisperwind Haven. A highlight of the enchanting Gondola cruise, the sea of clouds has long been a must-see destination, captivating visitors with its ethereal, dreamlike vistas.
Yet, few are aware that the Atrium of Reflections—often depicted in romantic tales—is not merely a creation of fiction, but the ruins of the highest spire of ancient Ragunna. To save its people, Napoli the Second invoked a miracle, turning the Dark Tide into the very sea of clouds that graces the land today.
The forgotten ruins of old Egla Town are now submerged beneath the sea of clouds.

[The Journey is the Destination] Embark Today!
It's worth noting that, although the reason remains unclear, the water level of Nimbus Sanctum has been steadily rising over the past decade, forcing the residents of Egla Town to move to the higher ground in the north.
Once, this area was a barren, undeveloped land, scattered with exposed boulders, and known as the Whisperwind Barrens.
However, the resourceful people of Egla Town began to build windmills that turned day and night, drawing water from the lower regions to nourish the land above. Their efforts transformed this rugged place into the thriving Whisperwind Haven we see today, where crops and flowers now flourish in the breeze.

[Column Memories] Voice of Travelers!
Your Egla column hasn't been updated since last Carnevale. It's just the same article over and over. You guys can't afford to pay the writer or something?
Could it be that no one's interested in Egla Town? Really? Am I actually right?

(A short novel published ten years ago.
"An outrageous best-seller, banned by the Order three times!"
"Only one-tenth of readers truly understand it—are you one of them?"
"Incredible! The Russellian's satire remains as insightful as ever, even after all these years!"
So reads the editor's recommendation page… Clearly, this book stirred up quite a bit of controversy a decade ago.)

Far out across the stormy waters filled with jagged ridges and giant beasts on the surface of Solaris lies a group of small, unregarded islands. On this archipelago, the exiles-descended cultures are so amazing that they still think a unified thought is a pretty neat idea. These islands have—or rather had a problem, which was this: most of the people on them were unhappy for pretty much of the time.

After retirement, I kept thinking back to that afternoon when my friend and I first met.
Ford Percival. He was an alien.
On his first day in Egla Town, he ate ten baton bread without paying anything. Before the Divine Envoys could punish him for theft, I quickly paid off his debt.
Since the prayer, the Oracle of Mercy had wandered in my mind in search of something to connect with—until I met him, the poor outlander. He must have been starving.
"Hi, I'm Ford. I'm an alien. I'm analyzing your weapons. Quite odd components."
He said after I saved him. "And what is this place?" he continued.
An alien? Oh, I'd heard this kind of tale once from someone who claimed to be from a federation. He said Solaris was actually a living tomato—a tomato that could turn, breathe, even dance. And aliens, apparently, were from other tomatoes, living or dead.
"Egla Town," I replied.
"Egla Town, good. Wait, what is that?" He pointed at the windmills in the distance.
"Those are windmills. A cluster of Cyclop windmills, Briareos." Born and raised in Egla, I replied almost instinctively.
"C-Cyclops! Ah, I know about those! I've seen them before! But my stars—you actually managed to kill them? How did you people pull that off? Are those auto-rotating arrays made from their dead bodies? And what exactly is Briareos? A cooling device? A propeller engine? Or something to open up a network channel?"

(Continued)

After hearing my explanation, the self-proclaimed alien Ford seemed completely fascinated by the Cyclops. His emotions became so agitated that he plopped down on the ground, muttering some unintelligible words while pointing at the windmills in the distance.
So it was true—no matter where they came from, no matter what "tomatoes" they hailed from, anyone who laid eyes on the scenery of Egla couldn't help but fall in love with the chivalric literature.
So I straightened up, took three steps forward, and adjusted the nonexistent necktie, then explained graciously, "Exactly! That's right! Once, a righteous knight guided us to defeat the giant. Before that, all the people and Echoes in Egla Town were driven to the high ground in the south, fleeing from the giant's threat. Now, that oppressor lies buried beneath the sea of flowers. We built majestic windmills to irrigate the flowers and the farmlands, and named our past home Briareos, in honor of that knight's heroic deeds!"
After hearing my speech, Ford sat frozen on the ground, as if ten thousand Cetus the Tidebreakers had roared at him all at once, shattering his perception.
After a long pause, he asked me in disbelief, "Do you still have knights here?"
What did he just ask me?
Praise be to Imperator!
I could finally deliver the ranked No. 1 answer in the Top 10 Most Satisfying Moments for Egla People.
Putting on a solemn expression like the Acolytes of the Order, I envisioned a halo of nobility above my head, envisioned the almighty Imperator spreading wings before me, envisioned myself crowning a laurel at the Carnevale, envisioned standing in the grand church, wielding a sword as I was knighted, relishing the reverent gazes of the noble lords of Ragunna!
I replied, stressing each word with great emphasis:
"OF COURSE—"
"However, there are too many outsiders who seek the path of knighthood. Are you confident enough to accept the trial?"
The alien named Ford, whose Tacet Mark was blinking along excitedly, quickly grabbed my calf and shook it furiously, as if clinging to a log in the midst of a drowning. He cried out, "I am! I am! Please guide me to the legendary knight! As long as I can return to the planet Russel and save my hometown, I am willing to pay any price!"

(The trial chapters end now. Please make a purchase to continue reading.)

(A feature on the culinary traditions of Ragunna.)

[Top Chef's Super Secrets]
Imagine yourself asking anyone on the streets of Ragunna, "Which restaurant is the best in Ragunna?"
Six out of ten will answer, "Trattoria Margherita!" Three will point to the family restaurant downtown, and the last one will say, "It's the place where the soft-tailed chef works!"
That's right! Such is the clout of Trattoria Margherita in Ragunna!
Amazing!
But what many don't know is that Trattoria Margherita is actually a family-run restaurant inspired by traditional Ragunna cuisine. From our investigation, we found that Egla Town still preserves this classic culinary tradition to this day. To maintain the special flavors of her dishes, Miss Margherita even takes time off to gather ingredients in Egla Town or Riccioli Islands!
Now, you might be wondering: "What? I can understand why Miss Margherita would go to Riccioli Islands for the fish harvest, but Egla Town? Isn't that a backwater town? And can the cuisine of Egla really be called Ragunna cuisine?"
Indeed, life in Egla isn't as thrilling as in the bustling Ragunna. People there live quietly, following the rhythm of nature. The town's trade and logistics are tied to Ragunna City. The people rise with the wind and rest by it, living a life shaped by windmills, wheat farms, and pastures.
But that's exactly why, for hundreds of years, the cuisine of Egla has remained unchanged. Here, the original flavors and cooking techniques of Ragunna have been preserved—using windmills to process crops and cooking food in traditional ways.
"This way, the ingredients and the food are especially precious! The cheese made from local pastures is creamy, and the meat is tender and flavorful! It's the perfect food to fill your belly!"
Miss Margherita commented during our interview.

[Comments from Special Guests]
Former Tax Envoy of the Order: The traditional cuisine is a remembrance of Rinascita's past. To forget it is to betray our heritage!
Orlando the Gourmet: The old man earlier sounded like he was chanting a slogan! What traditional cuisine? The bread from your town is as hard as a lethal weapon!

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part I)
...

At dawn, the Primus and I stood to bid farewell to the Pilgrim's Sail as it prepared to depart. Both the crowd and the acolytes watched with reverence as the believers boarded the ship. Only the most devout and courageous among them were chosen to embark on the Pilgrim's Sail, destined to meet the Sentinel in the distant sea.

For countless ages, Sentinel Imperator has rarely lingered in any one place, choosing instead to roam the seas, aiding vessels on their journeys. The Sentinel's guiding light has always led those lost upon the waves, helping them find their way back home or seek new lands for settlement. The Order believes that to face the storms and tides in search of the Sentinel's heavenly voice is one of the greatest honors a soul can aspire to.

Yet only those with practical experience can grasp the immense cost of each pilgrimage. Taxes and provisions are drawn from the commoners, skilled workers and sailors are taken from prominent families, and seasoned captains and chief mates are hired at great expense. All who embark on these treacherous seas are devout, but only those truly blessed by the Sentinel return with the promised glory and honor. Reflecting on history, the number of such fortunate souls is vanishingly small.

I have never questioned the purpose of the pilgrimage. My only concern is the immense cost it demands. Can we, in good conscience, allow these devoted believers to embark on a journey that burdens both mind and body? And as for our new Primus... What are his thoughts on this matter?

I looked to my side, surprised to find that my former seminary classmate, Lord Fenrico, had his face shrouded in a strange shadow.

...

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part II)
...

How has it come to this? After a sleepless night, I retreated to a secluded prayer room, seeking solace as I lay my confession before Sentinel Imperator. My hands trembled as I put these words to paper.

For a time, the Order ceased organizing large-scale pilgrimages, and the burdensome taxes were lifted. Though the people of Ragunna still honored the devotion of those who once sought the Sentinel across the distant seas, the Pilgrim's Sails had become a relic of the past. But everything changed after the bloody Carnevale... No, in truth, the shift began even earlier than that...

I still remember when the Primus delivered the order for correction, and I dutifully transcribed it: the Order would send violators of doctrine aboard the Pilgrim's Sails, stripping them of all official identities and setting them back onto the path of pilgrimage. Who could have foreseen that an act once meant to embody faith would come to serve as a form of punishment?

"The power of punishment and indoctrination shall be returned to the Sentinel," the Primus proclaimed to the assembled crowd. "Those transgressors who embark upon the pilgrimage in sincere repentance will, by their journey's end, be absolved of all transgressions and granted the Sentinel's forgiveness."

Yet no one truly knows if transgressors can fulfill their salvation, for no one has ever returned from the pilgrimage alive. "Those who commit acts of foolishness shall be sent to the Pilgrim's Sails"—this has become a steadfast law of the Order Penitentiary. Vandals defacing sacred statues, disloyal acolytes distorting doctrines, and even troupe members crafting satirical comedies—all have been condemned to the Pilgrim's Sails for their acts of blasphemy. Recently, however, familiar faces have joined their ranks, faces of those who had openly questioned the Primus's decrees.

I could have sworn my integrity on their faith and character, yet I stood by and watched as they were sent aboard the Pilgrim's Sails, doing nothing. No, it's no longer fitting to call them the Pilgrim's Sails. The common folk have given them a more appropriate name—the Fool's Sails, a vessel filled with those who have committed foolish acts.

Oh, Primus Fenrico... Is this the dream world you so passionately spoke of in the seminary?

...

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part III)
...

I was surprised at how calm I felt upon hearing the sentence from the Order Penitentiary. Perhaps my heart had grown as still as that of a dead person.

At dawn, like others before me, I was escorted by the Executors to board a Fool's Sail. Before the ship set sail, I glanced back at the port, only to find the Primus absent. Just as I expected, that man, now in control of unmatched power within the Order, has no need to concern himself with a fool stripped of his identity.

The Fool's Sails are nothing like the Pilgrim's Sails of old. Gone are the smooth, spacious decks and well-maintained sails. Instead, all I saw were rickety planks, loose screws, and splintered masts. The narrow cabins clearly lacked food and fresh water. I stared blankly at the other pilgrims around me. For now, we still manage to maintain some semblance of decorum and restraint, but I know that, before long, this ship will become nothing more than a cage filled with rampaging desires.

And even if we do reach the so-called destination, what awaits us there?

I once read the investigation reports sent back by the expatriate acolytes. That Penitent's End, shrouded in mist, is littered with the wrecks of Pilgrim's Sails. During those fateful voyages, the Fools who braved the storms never met the Sentinel. Instead, driven by the sea's undercurrents, they were cast ashore on that island, where the eerie glow of phosphorescence mingles with an unmistakable aura of death. I've even heard whispers of something far more terrifying lurking there, and the "Fire of Judgment"—a force so dreadful that even the Privy Council dares not speak of it.

...

Food is running out... Last night, someone lost control again, trying to lock themselves in the cabin to hoard the dwindling supplies...

O great Imperator, if you can hear my prayer, please grant us your final mercy through a storm. Absolve us from our misery, and let us... find peace at last.

(The remainder of the notes has been blurred by the seawater and is unreadable.)
InfoDisplay_102802004_Text: A Transgressor's Transcript (Part I) In the ancient era, long before Ragunna was founded, the distant seas of Rinascita were the Realm of A Thousand Islands. At that time, the Fisalia family was already well-versed in the ways of the ocean. We extracted toxins and medicines from deep-sea plants, harnessed vast underwater resources, and reveled in great fortune and widespread renown. Later, with the assault of the Lament, the civilization of the archipelago teetered on the brink of destruction and our family became one of the founders of the Ark, embarking on a quest to find a new settlement. The journey across the sea was treacherous. The fleets of the Ark were either swallowed by thick fog or torn apart by fierce storms. Yet, our family's Ark, guided by a heavenly voice, led the fleet to a lush archipelago, following the faint glow of a distant lighthouse. One of those islands would later become what is now Ragunna. The newly founded Ragunna was still in a state of flux. To strengthen the family's rule, our family head declared that the manifestation of ▇▇▇▇ was a symbol of the deep-sea faith and a response from the marine divinity to our devotion. This proclamation proved to be successful. As the number of believers grew, so too did the stability of our family's power. Later, some fishermen claimed that they had been assisted by ▇▇▇▇ during their fishing trips. This entity, long known as the Giant One, had existed for ages. Its shadow beneath the sea guided Ragunna's fishermen and fleets, helping them weather storms and bringing in harvests far greater than before. The Fisalia family was the original ruler of Ragunna, and we also laid the faith foundation of the Order. Yet, why have generations of family heads chosen to conceal this history? Why can't I remember Its name? Cursed be it, the wound... it is throbbing again. Something must be wrong with the air... I must find a safer place. The soldiers will never think to search for me in the tower. I must document this secret history... before it slips from my mind entirely... A Transgressor's Transcript (Part II) The fishermen referred to the shadow in the sea as ▇▇▇▇, and they would call upon its sacred name to receive its aid. Small miracles began to accumulate, forming a powerful current of faith. The common folk grew increasingly convinced that the Giant One was, indeed, ▇▇▇▇. As the family began to investigate, they were shocked to discover that these miraculous occurrences differed greatly from those recorded in the past. So, what was the true form of the Giant One the people had placed their faith in? And what, exactly, was the true object of our devotion? This mysterious faith was quietly reshaping the history of Ragunna, and it even threatened our family's control over the Order of the Deep. Only the Ark forebears and our family heads knew that ▇▇▇▇ should be the true form of ▇▇. Yet, with the preaching of the Order, the common folk, unaware of the truth, began to place their faith even more in ▇▇▇▇. Meanwhile, rumors spread that the true form of ▇▇▇▇ was that of a fish-like deity. What's even stranger was that those who heard these rumors began to dream of ▇▇▇▇ in the form of ▇▇. Is this text truly the same record I once read in the secret chamber of the family head? I have an unsettling feeling that my hands are writing down the history about ▇▇▇▇ on their own. Ah, I remember now... Yes, even I, who have never set sail on the sea, was drawn into that dream as I fled. Beneath the tranquil surface of the sea, a giant dark shadow loomed, and my fishing boat felt like a mere sampan before it... Impossible... That impure, blasphemous form could not have been the object of my faith all this time. I must reveal the truth to the world. A Transgressor's Transcript (Part III) After the death of Napoli the Second, the Order of the Deep elected a new Primus. The spread of the faith surpassed all previous reach. Yet, the doctrines proclaimed by the Acolytes were tainted by a dark mist. Everything related to ▇▇▇▇ began to twist—its statues, its anecdotes, and even its proverbs... No one has ever suspected this mass hallucination. No one has ever resisted the dissipation of the form, for "every drop of water will eventually return to the sea." Who is speaking in the "head" on my neck? Silence, you blasphemous thing! Where's my pen? No, it's in my hand. But is it truly my hand? Why is there black... blood dripping from it? In the face of these changes, our family remained eerily silent, even turning a blind eye to the Order slipping beyond our control. Many members of the Fisalia family were tormented by strange nightmares... They all saw the giant fish shadow beneath the sea and awoke in terror, screaming. (The text becomes illegible, and the paper is marked with scratches of unknown meaning.) I hear "sacred songs" flowing from my mouth. The sound of wet scratches echoes on the floor. The ancient blood still flows within me. IT is here... IT is everywhere... Some abandoned the family, becoming devout believers of the Order. Some ventured to Septimont and never spoke of the faith again, while others settled near the seaport, growing detached from the other forces. Oh, the poor Fisalias—once powerful, once surrounded by allies—reduced to this. Cast away the innate fears, and I no longer doubt that It is ▇▇▇▇, and ▇▇▇▇ is It—they are one and the same. In the depths of reason, I feel an indescribable joy. O my glorious Fisalia, the shadows of my people are approaching, guiding me to the deep sea. It is calling me. Praise be to ▇▇▇▇.
InfoDisplay_102802005_Text: Excerpts from The Hammer of Heresy (The pamphlet presents several radical opinions that appear to reflect the theories of an extreme school of thought.) What is witchcraft? And what is its true nature? The power of Resonance wielded by Resonators is known as a blessing from Sentinel Imperator. Devout followers of the Order are granted this blessing by adhering to its precepts, allowing them to channel the divine force through mortal bodies. Witchcraft, however, arises from vain desires—faithless souls, drawn by Leviathan, form a contract to practice forbidden arts. In doing so, they forsake the divine blessing bestowed upon them at birth and abandon their humanity, transforming into witches who seek to taint the mortal realm with profane power. The Divinity has shaped our world, and all that we hold dear flows from Their blessings. Yet witches, seduced by the Arch Enemy, pervert these divine creations into impure, disgraceful entities, crafting a false Resonance with them. The enemy's mark upon these witches is proof of their transgressions. With the aid of the Vessel of the Enemy, they can even transform into Tacet Discords, posing a grave threat to Imperator's faithful followers. Caution is essential, for anyone who craves freedom and worldly desires is vulnerable to becoming pawns of Leviathan. Thus, we must regularly cleanse and exorcise such souls. If we allow these heretics to grow unchecked, wielding their tainted power to defile the mortal realm, they will inevitably bring the Dark Tide upon Rinascita. It is the Order's duty to guide and govern them, ensuring they align with Imperator's divine will. Should they refuse to join the Order, swear loyalty to Imperator's statute, or diligently uphold its teachings, their misguided fate will be set right by the Pilgrim's Sails. We shall pray for them day and night, that they may be saved by our Sentinel Imperator. Praise be to Imperator. The Spy Network of the Order the Deep Ah, my friend, my companion on this quest for freedom and truth, I implore you—open this pamphlet only in a secure place, away from prying eyes. What I am about to reveal is crucial to your safety. Learn now how to identify the spies of the Order the Deep and evade their grasp. All Echoes bearing a golden halo upon their heads are spies of the Order the Deep, serving as "Angels." They are always seen alongside the Acolytes, serving as the Order's minions to take out the heretics. Rinascita, the Land of Echoes? Ha... not even the greatest satire could ever truly capture the utter absurdity of the reality we endure. First, you must beware of those lantern Echoes, known as Lucerna. Though they may appear harmless, they possess the ability to reveal so-called heretics hiding in the shadows of the night. Their light can illuminate the path ahead, yet it also serves as a blinding weapon, causing one to lose their sense of direction. There was once an instance where someone used Fae Ignis's Echo ability to remain concealed, only to be exposed under the unforgiving glow of a Lucerna's light. Next, there are the most commonly seen plaster statues, the infamous La Guardia, the most loyal guardians of the Order. Without commands from the Acolytes, they stand motionless, like silent statues. However, if you find yourself pursued by La Guardia, do not waste time fighting them. Instead, focus on locating the Acolyte of the Order Penitentiary who is issuing the command. Among all these minions, the most detestable is Vox Sanctus, perched high atop the church buildings. They serve as the Order's guards of honor. While they cannot move freely, they use their instruments to preach false doctrines day and night. These sermons infiltrate the souls of the Ragunnesi, poisoning their thoughts. Can you imagine that the children of Ragunna are forced to hear this nonsensical preaching the moment they are born into this world? Oppression by force may still leave room for resistance, but in Ragunna, how can one escape the spiritual chains that seep into every corner of life? A Letter of Complaint on Heresy Esteemed Lord Acolyte, I, Charles Tornatore, hereby report a heretical action—an underground troupe by the name of Panacea, which has dared to reenact the banned play The Flying Ragunnesi, adding numerous malicious metaphors and imagery of blasphemy. I have transcribed the following lines to the best of my memory: "The Primus's words are like pickled spells. Even a Gondola will tingle upon hearing them." —From Act I, Scene 1 Can't the baton bread in my hand be strong enough to smash our enemies of faith? —From Act I, Scene 3 (Note: This line, spoken by an Acolyte, degrades the Order's holy instrument, referring to it as mere bread.) By Imperator above, please witness our love, as beautiful as the morning light. —From Act II, Scene 1 (Note: This line marks the elopement of the male and female protagonists.) ... I regret that I cannot recall all the blasphemous lines from the play. How dare these individuals defile our noble faith in such a manner? Though they hid behind masks during the performance, I was able to identify them by their forms and voices. It is no surprise that they serve the Montelli family (A detailed list of names is attached). Praise be to Imperator.
InfoDisplay_102802006_Text: The Old Codex of Holy Rituals Chapter 2 Verse 17 2:17 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] And lo, from the storm, the mass heard the voice of Imperator. 2:18 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] And Imperator said, Come ye forth, to the east. 2:19 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] And Sentinel Imperator cast forth a light through the rain and the waves. The mass followed the light and sailed through the mist and the storm. 2:20 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] And the light, it came from the lighthouse upon the distant archipelago, where the warm currents meet, and where spices grow, and where golden fruit trees abound. 2:21 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] But from the mist behind them, dreadful Tacet Discords did pursue and tread upon the thunder, and the people cried out in wailing. 2:22 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] Then said Sentinel Imperator, I shall bring salvation. 2:23 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] And the Genesis Nexus cast forth a radiant light, and the Tacet Discords were swallowed up by the lighthouse. And when Sentinel Imperator called them forth once more, they became Divine Envoys. 2:24 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] And Sentinel Imperator said, wherever the Genesis Nexus shines, there shall the Divine Envoys dwell. The Genesis Nexus shall be my hand. I am the lighthouse of Rinascita, Sentinel Imperator. 2:25 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] For hundreds of years, the multitude hath followed Their precepts. 2:26 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] The Divine Envoys have shown their strength to uphold Their will. 2:27 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] To the followers, regard these as Imperator's blessing and spirit. 2:28 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] Love the Divine Envoys, as ye love your family, your brothers and sisters, and your neighbors. 2:29 [The Codex of Holy Rituals] We carry out the holy sacraments in memory of this. The New Codex of Holy Rituals Chapter 5 Verse 2 5:03 [The New Codex of Holy Rituals] They desired to deliver the Oracle, and so They inscribed the sacred words upon the oak tree, and from the Oracle, the first Viscum Berry did grow. 5:04 [The New Codex of Holy Rituals] The berry is the essence of Imperator's wisdom. And so shall we be as brothers, and none shall be set apart. 5:11 [The New Codex of Holy Rituals] Such is the spirit. The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation Chapter 1 Verse 9 1:09 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] On that day, Napoli's brows and his hair were white like wool, as white as snow, and his eyes were as a flame of fire. 1:10 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] And They granted unto Napoli the lantern, like bronze glowing in a furnace, and the lantern echoed with the voices of the Divine Envoys. 1:11 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] Napoli lifted the lantern high in his return, like the sun shining in all its brilliance. 1:12 [The Codex of Holy Rituals: Revelation] And the Tacet Discords of the Dark Tide bowed before him. InfoDisplay_102802007_Text: A Comprehensive Study of the History of Ragunnesi Drama (with Commentary) A Comprehensive Study of the History of Ragunnesi Drama: The Evolution of Tribal Cultural Fusion and Faith Systems Written by: DeLillo Quentin Proposed Grant: Ragunna Dramatic Association Regional Research Project - Aspire Scholars Grant Avinoleum Theological Seminary, Ragunna, Rinascita Abstract: This paper reviews recent research trends and developments regarding the origins of drama culture in the Ragunna and Septimont regions, with a particular focus on advancements in the "archaeology of drama" over the past decade. Drawing on the diverse research and perspective studies from the New Federation in recent years, the paper also incorporates insights from Huanglong's archaeological experience in studying historical relics. The case studies selected focus primarily on classic plays and significant historical events. The findings suggest that Ragunnesi drama culture originated from narrative performances that documented the history and life of island tribes. Keywords: history of drama, cultural studies, review, folklore studies, archaeology ...(Some of the pages are missing) As illustrated in key literature such as Chronicles of Avinoleum and The Golden Bough, the origin of drama is directly tied to the faith of Sentinel Imperator. However, technical studies of stage design, costumes, makeup, masks, and props, as found in both historical and modern literature, as well as translated foreign texts, reveal that much remains to be explored regarding the evolution of drama as a reflection of life and folklore. For instance, the Montelli Culture Foundation's Cultural Characteristics and Cultural Reconstruction in Translation: A Case Study of the Journey to Rinascita Collected in Huanglong examines the transition from folk traditions to their textual and stage representations in drama, focusing on the evolution of the translated texts. Seminary Commentary: Please do not submit the anecdotal piece for Almanacs and the Occult to our foundation. Additionally, food security must be more strictly managed to prevent potential nervous breakdowns among students caused by consuming spoiled bell crabs. ...(Some of the pages are missing) The people of Rinascita during the Age of a Thousand Islands used costumes to represent the origins of different tribes, masks to symbolize ancestors and totems, and various tribal languages to interact and communicate with one another during the Carnevale in the form of drama. This process continued until a fusion and mutual understanding among the tribes was achieved. After numerous adaptations and reinterpretations of folklore and legends, it eventually evolved into the prototype of the Ragunnesi drama, which remains popular today. Mentor Commentary: It is recommended to omit some of the details and avoid excessive research, as the paper will be reviewed by the Chamber of Enlightenment of the Order. A Study on the Evolution of Drama Costumes and Stage Design (This handwritten notebook is almost completely torn, with only a few pages from the Epilogue remaining.) Epilogue: I would like to dedicate this paper to my friends who have supported me, to those who have secretly provided invaluable literature for my research, to the work of my father, DeLillo Quentin, to the exile granted to me by the Order of the Deep, and to the expulsion by Avinoleum Theological Seminary. This paper, titled "A Study on the Evolution of Drama Costumes and Stage Design," has taken four years to complete, from its inception to the eve of my exile, and I have finally finished the first draft. I hope my friends can read it, as I originally intended. Tomorrow morning, I will leave Ragunna aboard the Pilgrim's Sail, just as my father did, in search of the Sentinel—Praise be to Imperator! If I survive, I hope you, the omnipresent Imperator, will guide my way. ...When I was a child, my father, DeLillo, said to me before he left, "Little Quentin, do you know what humans are?" I knew that would be my father's last words to me, so I replied that I didn't know. Father then said, "Keep doing your best, Mario Quentin. Humans are a blade of thinking seagrass." I didn't understand why humans would be compared to a blade of seagrass. But now, I think I understand what father meant—don't stop thinking and don't stop searching. The islands of the past were destroyed in the Lament. Under Imperator's guidance, our ancestors boarded the Ark and voyaged far, eventually establishing Rinascita on the land it now occupies. During the Age of a Thousand Islands, to commemorate their lost homes and honor their tribespeople in the Lament, people began to wear the costumes of their tribes and masks symbolizing their ancestors and totems. As concluded in Chapter 4 of this paper, the culture of drama has never been a blessing promised by the Order. Rather, it is a commemoration and symbol developed independently by the people of Rinascita. But are we truly just a blade of seagrass? If so, there must be a distinction between the seagrass that flows with the waves and those that can think independently, right? People praise the name of Imperator for its mercy and its encompassing nature, for preserving the culture that unites people from different tribes, helping them merge and support one another. They praise Imperator for the will to unite the vast patch of seagrasses to defy the currents of the Lament. Praise be to Imperator! We exalt you! But have the Ragunnesi of today truly executed your true will? Ah, great Imperator! I don't want to die... I really don't... I wish I could attend the Carnevale one more time... I'm truly terrified... Please, don't turn me into a blade of seagrass tomorrow! Laurel and Sword (Part I) Laurel and Sword: On the Divine Imagery in The Golden Bough Journal Title: Ragunna Sea Breeze Drama Society Research Journal, Volume 1 Category: Literary Studies, Literary Theory, Theater, The Golden Bough The Golden Bough, a Ragunnesi narrative epic rich in history and deeply influenced by primitive religious culture, is renowned for its prominent theatrical elements. The epic begins with pastoral plays that draw on the primitive beliefs and customs of various tribes during the Age of a Thousand Islands. As the story unfolds, these diverse narratives converge under the guidance of Sentinel Imperator. The author employs the perspectives of the Divine Envoys to provide Imperator's view, allowing the characters to assume their roles in classical plays. Throughout the work, recurring symbols of religion and totems appear, echoing metaphors commonly found in traditional plays. The use of these theatrical elements has helped establish the epic as a beloved classic, cherished by both officials and commoners in Ragunna. Furthermore, it embeds the author's profound reflections on the will behind the Oracle delivered by Sentinel Imperator, as well as the social changes occurring in the region of Rinascita. ...(Some of the pages are missing) One of the most commendable scenes in The Golden Bough is the concluding Scene 3, where five storylines dramatically converge at the climax of the Carnevale: the Holy Forest of the Fagaceae Peninsula, the Order of Ragunna, the Keepers of Secrets in Thessaleo Fells, the successor of the governor in Septimont, and the gladiators, all merging in a grand finale. In this scene, the author masterfully interweaves characters and plotlines, capturing the unique allure of a grand historical tragicomedy. This convergence in Scene 3 has served as a template, inspiring countless plays thereafter. The scene's influence owes much to its intricate plot design, which displays a skillful technique that sets a standard in narrative structure. Beyond the theoretical framework of the work itself, this design—where each element reflects the core theme and draws from historical settings—has solidified this epic as a timeless classic, maintaining its relevance and reverence across cultural shifts in literary history. (See Note 23) The Golden Bough is recognized as the earliest work of art to connect tribal folklore with the Sentinel (see Note 24). In the climactic Scene 3 of the Carnevale, the five masks stand together, each pursuing their own faith, when Sentinel Imperator descends from above, bestowing the laurel upon the chosen Enlightened One—the main protagonist on stage. This ritual has since become a lasting cultural emblem in the hearts of the people of Rinascita. From this scene onward, every heroic journey must conclude with the ritual of "being laureated," whether the hero takes on the role of an actor on stage or a playwright behind the scenes during the Carnevale. Laurel and Sword (Part II) Laurel and Sword: On the Divine Imagery in The Golden Bough Journal Title: Ragunna Sea Breeze Drama Society Research Journal Category: Literary Studies, Literary Theory, Theater, The Golden Bough (Continued) The reason for Sentinel Imperator's descent at the climax of the Carnevale in The Golden Bough remains an open question, one largely unexamined in the epic itself or in related research. Historically, the prevailing view in the Seminary held that the Laureate must be the individual who most aligns with Rinascita's ideals and resonates with the Sentinel—not driven by dramatic passion or ulterior motives. For a long time, this perspective dominated studies of The Golden Bough and the broader field of Laureate literature, with the laurel seen as a symbol of immense honor and the embodiment of Rinascita's collective will. (See Note 25) However, following the cultural events after the Seminary incident, the Laureate's symbol and performances are now seen as expressions of the Sentinel's divine will—the guiding force behind delivering the Oracle and unifying the doctrines. The image of laurel has also come to represent this sacred intent. The author raises an intriguing question: given this interpretation, could the selection of the Laureate itself be seen as an indoctrination of freedom—a concept seemingly at odds with The Golden Bough? Can freedom, once indoctrinated, still be considered freedom? ...(Some of the pages are missing) [23] Charlie Welbeck, "The History of Reforms on the Rinascita Drama Aesthetics," published by Avinoleum Theological Seminary Culture Journal. [24] Mario Quentin, "A Study on the Evolution of Drama Costumes and Stage Design," published by Foreign Culture Studies Publishing House. [25] Cosimo Sorrentino, "A Study on the Readership of The Golden Bough," published by Ragunna Dramatic Association.

Timeworn Logbook 1
Logbook_Number_#00
Mom, have you ever seen a Nimbus Wraith? I saw one for the first time today, and it was incredible.
I'm so excited. I don't really know who to share this with, so I'm writing it down here.
Today feels like a real turning point for me.
Starting today, I'm working for the Montelli family. I'm part of the Montellis now, and from now on, people will call me by that name.
The gate to Rinascita has finally opened for me.
Even though I'm in a cabin right now, thousands of miles away from home, as long as I'm working under the Montelli name and wearing this uniform, maybe one day I'll have my own place in the Montelli Quarter in Ragunna.
Mom, I think I finally get why the Montelli name is so well-known across Rinascita.
While other noble families sell positions or goods, the Montellis sell hope.
I'm about to get really busy, and I'm adjusting to the job just fine. The only problem is there's just me as the security guard on board, so there's no one to talk to.
I'm going to work hard, and when I come back, I'll bring you to Ragunna so you can enjoy life here too.

Timeworn Logbook 2
Logbook_Number_#17
Mom, I miss you.
It's pretty misty here, and whenever it's like this, I can't help but think back to when I was little, back when we were together.
We used to live in a house out in the countryside. It was a thatched cottage, and in the summer, I could hear the dried hay on the roof crackling as the sun beat down. In the winter, the walls would get damp.
Inside, the house had a narrow hallway that led to the kitchen, where a broken lightbulb, somehow always mysteriously fixed, hung from the ceiling. The exposed wires were wrapped in black tape.
Along the hallway were two rooms. I slept in the smaller one, the one on the north side. The gauzy curtains, printed with the sacred verses of the Order, always felt a little eerie at night. When I couldn't sleep, I'd sneak out to the narrow hallway. It didn't matter if I kept my eyes open or closed. With my back against the damp walls, it was pitch black, and I couldn't even see my own breath.
The wind tried to sneak in through the cracks, and the door frame seemed to shrink. The old wires were starting to tear, and the damp air pressed against the bricks. My hair brushed against the wall, and behind it, a patch of quilt slowly shifted. All these sounds tangled together in my head, floating from my ears to my skin, then rushing back inside, shaking my bones with a soft, mesmerizing tremor.
I can't shake this feeling of dampness that echoes in my mind. Today, it's here again.
I just passed through the misty barrier on our route. It felt like an unsettling dream.
But don't worry about me. The safety manual says this mist can cause hallucinations, but it's harmless. I've made it through safely. Now, I need to check the inventory again, just in case someone took something while I was dreaming.
I really miss you, Mom. Don't forget what I promised. Once I've made my name here, I'll bring you to Ragunna.

Timeworn Logbook 3
Logbook_Number_#29
Mom, don't worry. I'll be home and see you soon.
The day before yesterday was so cloudy, and I bet the Nimbus Wraiths were feeling pretty gloomy. We weren't supposed to set sail, but with the auction coming up, I have to make sure the item gets delivered on time.
This mission was given to me by the Montellis, and I can't let them down.
It's a bit of a detour, but since all the ships have already left and the Order sent Lucerna on board, I think it should be fine.
Don't worry. The Montelli family added more people to the crew, and with the Order's presence, everything will be okay. Yeah, it'll be fine.
I should tell you something to lift your spirits. Once I'm done with this job, I should have some time off to come and visit you.
Even though my job keeps me in the cabins, I get to see a lot of interesting things along the route.
Here, they don't use words like sunny or cloudy to describe the weather. Instead, they use emotions, which is kind of interesting, don't you think?
When it's "happy," we get to see rainbows, and the Nimbus Wraiths even dance under them.
When it's "gloomy," like today, it's cloudy, and we usually get to take the rest of the day off.
A "forced smile" is when it's sunny, but with a hint of rain. At times like that, the train picks up speed on purpose, and some of my colleagues will start telling loud jokes from the back of the train.
When it's "sorrowful," it rains, and the train moves very slowly.
"Unhappy" weather means thunder or strong winds. On days like that, we definitely take the day off. I just sleep through it.
And then there's "angry" weather, which is the scariest. The entire sea of clouds turns red. If we encounter that in the middle of the journey, our superiors make us wear soundproof earmuffs to work.
According to the route map, we'll be passing through a place called the Atrium of Reflections. I'd never heard of it before, but the seniors say we usually avoid it unless it's absolutely necessary.
I'll be careful, though. Don't worry about me. It's just a small challenge. Tough jobs need to be done, right?
As long as I put in the effort, I know I'll get the reward I deserve. Just wait for me, Mom. I'll bring you to Ragunna.

Timeworn Logbook 4
Logbook_Number_#31
Mom, when I get back, can I just hug you for a bit?
I've gone through the entire safety manual, but I didn't find anything about the situation I'm facing right now.
Do you remember, Mom? When I was little, and the wind picked up at night, I was always scared. It was actually because of the gauzy curtain in my room. It had the patterns of people praying in the Order embroidered on it. When the night breeze blew, the shadows of those figures would flutter as if they might break apart.
I thought I saw them in real life just now. A group of people was kneeling by the side of the train, as if they were praying with their heads lowered.
They were staring at the train, and I couldn't bring myself to look back. They were mumbling something... I finally found the soundproof earmuffs.
It's okay. Maybe I'm just too nervous. The Lucernas from the Order are still here. They'll figure something out.
By Imperator above, we will arrive safely.
(The words are illegible due to being soaked in water.)
...Mom... I will... bring you... to Ragunna.
By Imperator above
By Imperator above
By Imperator above
By Imperator above... I'm safe!
(Trembling handwriting)
I made it! I'm safe now!
But what exactly... are these things...?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_28_2: Why is this place upside down?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_28_3: I believe it's to prevent them from falling to the ground.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_28_5: Tacet Discords. The Dark Tide. And these ruins themselves.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_28_6: I imagine it's also a symbolic reminder that our beliefs have been turned on their head.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_28_7: This view matches with what I saw at the time.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_28_8: Until you get used to the gravity here, I suggest we travel via "Phaom."
Main_Linaxita_2_4_28_9: It's the name I gave to a Gondola.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_29_2: Oh, dear... I completely forgot about this...
Main_Linaxita_2_4_29_3: How about I go with Cartethyia first?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_29_4: How about I go with Cantarella first?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_29_5: How about I go with Abby first?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_29_6: Can we make room for one more?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_29_7: It seems I get to enjoy a free ride after you've scouted the paths ahead.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_29_9: Now's not the time to be so careless after that promise you just made to Cartethyia.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_29_10: You should focus on learning more about this place from her. I'll be watching with great interest to see what you come up with.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_29_12: Isn't Abby... living inside your Tacet Mark?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_29_13: Well, then, the two of you go on ahead.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_29_14: Greed will get you punished, you know.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_29_15: I'm afraid Phaom would refuse that suggestion...
Main_Linaxita_2_4_29_16: The two of you can go on ahead.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_31_4: Are you afraid of knowing the answer?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_31_5: I am afraid... but not of the answer. I fear never finding one at all.
LNXTSJZL_31_1: This book documents some of the Fisalia family's history.
LNXTSJZL_31_2: I'm not sure if you're interested in this mysterious family, but when we first arrived, we also heard some strange things about them...
LNXTSJZL_32_1: These seem to be the former privy councilor's notes. From what's written, a Pilgrim's Sail carried him away.
LNXTSJZL_32_2: I believe you know this history better than I do... Here, you can have this book.

HelpText_180_Content:
[About]
O Rover guided by the tides, you have banished the shadows of war in Jinzhou and crossed the boundaries of time on Mt. Firmament. When you stood upon the secluded shores, did you hear the gospel carried on the tempest winds, echoing across the stormy sea? Did you glimpse the unparalleled splendor that lies within the fabled land of the Echoes? Now, steel your heart and embark on a journey into the unknown, brave the storm, and carve a path to Rinascita.

[Eligibility]
Reach Union Level 14 and Complete Main Quest "Chapter I Act III Ominous Star."

[Event Rules]
After Main Quest Chapter II becomes available, eligible players as per above may play said Chapter regardless of their current Main Quest progress.

Chapter II progress is saved separately from Chapter I progress. Taking on Chapter II early does not affect your progress in Chapter I.

*For the most optimal experience, we recommend completing "Chapter I Act VIII:  To the Shore's End” before starting “Chapter II: Prologue."

[Event Rewards]

Each stage rewards can be claimed once only.
After the event concludes, rewards for cleared stages will be distributed via mail.

Character_Rococo_82_1: Are you okay? Where does it hurt?

LGNCZST_1411_1: Ah, finally. I can tell at a glance that you are not an ordinary person.
LGNCZST_1411_2: You... You must be a Bloom Bearer from the Black Shores, right?
LGNCZST_1411_3: Who are you? How did you know?
LGNCZST_1411_4: You are a Bloom Bearer, more Bloom Bearer than I.
LGNCZST_1411_5: Mr. Aalto was right. Bloom Bearers attract other Bloom Bearers!
LGNCZST_1411_6: Sorry, I forgot to introduce myself first. My name's Ariosto, and I am the undercover Bloom Bearer sent here to investigate Rinascita's recent issues.
LGNCZST_1411_7: Are you the only one they sent here?
LGNCZST_1411_8: Are there any other Bloom Bearers here?
LGNCZST_1411_9: The Black Shores has also sent other Bloom Bearers to Rinascita, but to keep things under the radar of the Order, we decided to split up.
LGNCZST_1411_10: If you head southeast toward Septimont, you'll likely run into some of our colleagues. Compared to Ragunna, Bloom Bearers enjoy a bit more freedom there—less surveillance and fewer rules to follow.
LGNCZST_1411_11: But... how should I put it? Things aren't quite as smooth in Septimont. Our operations face their own set of challenges, and the Bloom Bearers' work there hasn't been progressing as well as we'd hoped.
LGNCZST_1411_12: As you know, the Black Shores is a neutral organization, so we don't have the right to meddle in their affairs without the consent of the local officials.
LGNCZST_1411_13: Our relationship with Rinascita's city-states is… well, "delicate" is one way to put it. We've been providing warnings about the Lament crisis—Ragunna being the prime example, of course.
LGNCZST_1411_14: By the way... Come closer, gotta keep our voice low for this... Have you run into any... obstructions from the Order during your mission?
LGNCZST_1411_17: I see. It happened to me as well. On the surface, Ragunna appears peaceful, but behind the scenes, the Order has been plotting something.
LGNCZST_1411_18: People from the Order was hot on my tail when I was investigating this matter, and even had my Terminal taken from me. Luckily the Montellis extended a helping hand...
LGNCZST_1411_19: It was the same Ms. Carlotta who told me that a member of the Black Shores would be arriving in Ragunna soon. I decided to find {Male=him;Female=her} quickly and share the information I have.
LGNCZST_1411_20: I borrowed this costume and a mask from the Montelli to blend in with the crowd, so I could get back to the city during the Carnevale. Well, at least my hard work finally paid off.
LGNCZST_1411_22: How could they treat us like this!
LGNCZST_1411_23: Us Bloom Bearers, we endure hardship, but the Lament must be stopped at all costs! That's our Bloom Bearer Creed!
LGNCZST_1411_24: You must already have some sense of Ragunna's situation. Now, let me share a wild thought with you...
LGNCZST_1411_25: You saw that Sentinel statue in Ragunna, right? That statue is strikingly different from the appearance of Sentinel Imperator we recorded in the Tethys System.
LGNCZST_1411_26: Now, take a deep breath—because I'm about to say something big. What if, just what if... the people of Ragunna have been believing in a false Sentinel all along?
LGNCZST_1411_27: Wait... Enough talk for today. I can't shake the feeling that we're being watched.
LGNCZST_1411_28: My mission isn't finished. I'll stay in Rinascita and continue digging into their historical records about the Sentinel. My next stop is Whisperwind Haven. If fate allows, we'll meet again.
LGNCZST_1412_1: My mission isn't finished. I'll stay in Rinascita and continue digging into their historical records about the Sentinel. My next stop is Whisperwind Haven. If fate allows, we'll meet again.
kamola_shengtai_1_1: In Ragunna, there's never a shortage of secluded corners untouched by the masses. Yet somehow, you found me here. What a...
kamola_shengtai_1_3: I had a gut feeling I'd find you here.
kamola_shengtai_1_4: Hehe, fate has a funny way of leading us exactly where our hearts want to be, don't you think, Cat's Eye?
kamola_shengtai_1_5: It seems I'm not the only one who finds our time together hard to forget, am I? What do you say, Cat's Eye?
kamola_shengtai_1_7: Or perhaps, you already have plans with someone else?
kamola_shengtai_1_8: My answer is no to both questions.
kamola_shengtai_1_9: If someone were to approach me with a special drink right now, I wouldn't decline a conversation.
kamola_shengtai_1_10: But at least when I came here, I simply wanted some fresh air.
kamola_shengtai_1_11: The day is beautiful. The performers' melodies drift from the opera house, and the streets are alive with chatter and shouts of people.
kamola_shengtai_1_12: The city and its people shimmer—golden, vibrant, precious.
kamola_shengtai_1_13: In this fleeting moment, I can forget about the troubles.
kamola_shengtai_1_14: It seems family matters have been weighing on your mind?
kamola_shengtai_1_15: What's troubling you? If you need to talk, I'm all ears.
kamola_shengtai_1_16: Oh, you know how it is—endless deliberations, meticulous planning. There are a lot of things to consider.
kamola_shengtai_1_17: Like... My new dress from Nyarla's? What to wear for the next ball? Or perhaps which treasures to bid for at the auction?
kamola_shengtai_1_19: Capollo... He has been disowned and dealt with. It's left me with a tangle of new challenges to manage.
kamola_shengtai_1_20: My priorities remain the same: doing whatever that benefits the family. But now, with this new role entrusted to me, I carry new responsibilities—and with them, new strengths.
kamola_shengtai_1_21: As the next head of the family, it's my duty to face these responsibilities head-on, and to shape myself into the leader this position demands.
kamola_shengtai_1_22: But before this fleeting moment of peace is stolen away by duty, on an afternoon like this—
kamola_shengtai_1_23: Will you sit with me, Cat's Eye? Share a drink, share a bite?
kamola_shengtai_1_24: Let's set aside the "codes" hidden behind every glass for once. Like ordinary folk, we'll just savor the flavors for what they are, as they were meant to be.
kamola_shengtai_1_27: Thankfully, you have no pressing matters to attend to. On such a peaceful afternoon, sharing this moment with Carlotta feels like the right choice.
kamola_shengtai_1_28: Drinking during the day? You hesitate, questioning whether this is wise with your other commitments. Though you must decline her offer this time, perhaps you'll accept the next.
kamola_shengtai_2_1: A peaceful afternoon like this is always a delight, gilded in golden sunlight.
kamola_shengtai_2_2: To match this serenity, would you care to try a special blend?
kamola_shengtai_2_3: A special blend? How special are we talking?
kamola_shengtai_2_4: I think I've seen something like that on the menu before.
kamola_shengtai_2_5: Oh? Are you referring to the "codes" scattered around our usual meeting places and open-air bars?
kamola_shengtai_2_6: Those are certainly impressive, but not quite what I had in mind. I'm referring to a blend inspired by my codename, "Opal."
kamola_shengtai_2_7: Like the "Scarlet Velvet Ribbon" tied to Scarlet Velvet?
kamola_shengtai_2_9: "Opal" is more than just a drink—it's your key to reach me. Order it at any bar in Rinascita, and the Montelli network will ensure your message finds me.
kamola_shengtai_2_10: Of course, you could also order it to flaunt our bond. It'll grant you the protection of Montelli.
kamola_shengtai_2_11: Why? Because its recipe is a secret known only to me and a select few Montellis.
kamola_shengtai_2_12: Will you share this secret with me?
kamola_shengtai_2_13: Your secret is safe with me.
kamola_shengtai_2_14: Hehe, there's no need for promises. I've already placed my trust in you, completely.
kamola_shengtai_2_15: Alright, then. Here's the recipe—listen closely. White rum, rose nectar, pomegranate juice, a pinch of black pepper, and a touch of fritillaria powder.
kamola_shengtai_2_19: Alright, I'll repeat it for you. White rum, rose nectar, pomegranate juice, a pinch of black pepper, and a touch of fritillaria powder.
kamola_shengtai_2_20: Be sure to remember it well.
kamola_shengtai_2_21: What would it take to create a special blend?
kamola_shengtai_2_23: You mean a signature drink named after you, {PlayerName}?
kamola_shengtai_2_24: Let's come up with one, then. Feel free to choose from any flavor or color, or select a symbol that resonates with you.
kamola_shengtai_2_25: No limits—let your creativity shape your perfect beverage. You'll find it in the bars once you make your choice.
kamola_shengtai_2_26: Something icy and clear, sharp enough to focus the mind.
kamola_shengtai_2_27: Something daring and strange—something no one else would try.
kamola_shengtai_2_28: What kind of beverage am I to you?
kamola_shengtai_2_29: ...You've always felt a bit distant to me, whether you're making decisions or fighting. It fits the first impression I had of you.
kamola_shengtai_2_30: Oh? I didn't expect you'd go for an unusual blend. It might actually work pretty well as a "code."
kamola_shengtai_2_31: My opinion? Hmm, that's hard to say... Maybe something with a base of herbs and fruity flavors, rather than a pure grain spirit.
kamola_shengtai_2_32: It reminds me of the quiet kindness tucked away beneath your remarkable strength.
kamola_shengtai_2_33: But there's no need to rush. You'll have plenty of time to decide what kind of blend embodies you best.
kamola_shengtai_2_34: And before that, shall we savor this moment?
kamola_shengtai_2_35: You understand her unspoken message—some questions aren't meant to be answered right away.
kamola_shengtai_2_36: She wants to preserve this moment of tranquility, untouched by worry or haste. By your side, she feels at peace, and she hopes you feel the same.
kamola_shengtai_2_37: Time seems to pause between you. Without exchanging another word, you hold each other's gaze. In this silence, you and Carlotta become what she just described—a golden shimmer, vibrant and fleeting, yet infinitely precious.
kamola_shengtai_3_1: Such a peaceful, warm afternoon... It's spent well enough simply basking in the sunshine.
kamola_shengtai_4_1: Good to see you again, Cat's Eye.
kamola_shengtai_4_2: You've found me in my little corner once more.
kamola_shengtai_4_4: The sunshine is as pleasant as ever today.
kamola_shengtai_4_5: It seems you've mastered the secret of finding me.
kamola_shengtai_4_6: Then stay and share another afternoon with me, won't you?
kamola_shengtai_4_7: Yes. Like I said before, a peaceful afternoon such as this is always soothing.
kamola_shengtai_4_9: Let us savor this serenity together.

Main_Linaxita_2_4_52_14: But if you say so, I can offer you a strong elixir. Care to give it a try?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_52_16: Oh I insist. Here, take this.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_55_10: None but the Master shall ever have the right to command you to bend the knee.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_4: I should ask you that! What did you do just now, huh?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_5: I was dozing when bam! Outta nowhere a giant blue ball landed on top of me.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_7: I'm guessing putting Tyrvine on the pedestal has something to do with it.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_8: Oh, hey! It smells just as "unnatural" as that big gigantor back in Jinzhou.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_10: The Sentinel of Jinzhou... If what our little Echo friend says is true, then the frequency that entered your Tacet Mark could be Imperator's powers.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_11: Huh? But the Sentinel isn't even here.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_12: The power to split and manipulate space...
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_13: It is reminiscent of the moment of Tyrvine's creation. Only this time the place of confinement has become your Tacet Mark.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_14: But why would it do that?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_15: I believe it was meant for the "true" Maiden.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_16: Under the right circumstances, the one to wield this sword and enter the Sonoro Sphere would be the Sentinel's Resonator, the Blessed Maiden.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_17: The Sentinel entrusted Their power to the Resonator so that she could lend assistance when the corruption of the Threnodian altered Them. Quite logical, isn't it?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_18: You don't seem too thrilled about it.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_19: If Imperator set this in motion, then Their original plan has already failed.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_20: Cartethyia, that means your guidance holds the key now.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_23: Is there anything else you remember?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_24: I... just remembered the day I was crowned by the Order, and the moment the Dark Tide descended upon us...
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_28: But I didn't see the Dark Tide.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_29: That is all I can remember...
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_31: You witnessed it as well, Cantarella?
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_32: No. I only saw fragmented, blurry images...
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_33: They seemed to belong to other places within the Sonoro Sphere.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_34: I believe this is where we should rest. We'll wait until sunrise.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_36: We can take this time to think about the clues.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_37: You're the one who needs rest most of all.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_38: After all, it's still only a possibility that the frequency you absorbed is the Sentinel's powers. Rest now, to ensure it doesn't take a toll on you.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_39: I'm gonna hit the sack as well.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_56_40: Boy, it's so cramped in here...
Main_Linaxita_2_4_62_8: Go ahead, it's no use now that it's out of the pedestal... its energy is gone.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_62_9: It may still come in handy.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_62_10: ...I'll add you in my Terminal. Call me if you need help.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_62_11: Hehe... I just might ring you up once things are settled.
Main_Linaxita_2_4_62_12: You open your Terminal and exchange contact information. Cantarella leaves with Tyrvine.
